review_scope: Bounded source/assertion review. Parent findings and gate-results supersede draft execution statements. No whole-clause certification.

features.normative_effect: The PDF clauses provide information usable to substitute when a program is unavailable, but do not mandate substitute behavior for an unreadable program. §9.9 defines embedded-program organization/conformance; §9.7.4.2 and §9.7.5.2 constrain composite selection and Identity-H/V combinations.
features.verdict: Behavior is an owner-ratified product choice (A837/Q837, ADR 2870), not a reader requirement directly imposed by §9.5/§9.8.1. The simple-font test proves some ink/text, but its hand-built file has no xref and no recovery assertion; it does not provide an independent no-program route control or prove equal advances/geometry. Composite no-ToUnicode case is described as Adobe-Identity while fixture actually declares Registry Adobe / Ordering Identity; validity/routing should be verified from implementation and exact xref before relying on it. Identity-H no-program negative control is otherwise useful.
features.test_changes_since_prior: Three new integration modules/tests were added at this comparison. unreadable_program_substitute.rs and substitute_unreached_codes.rs construct PDFs without xref tables. refused_font_metrics.rs changed its fixture interpretation to inspect LoadedFont::metrics_only directly and added an assertion that the page reports substitute use; it no longer verifies the displayed next-font origin in the updated tests.
residuals: No independent valid-xref behavioral pair demonstrates unreadable-program fallback equals the same dictionary with no program while keeping the refusal visible.
Composite fallback test skips when the machine does not offer an addressable substitute, so it is conditional coverage, not universally asserted.

features.normative_effect: Table 109 requires dictionary widths to be consistent with the embedded program's actual widths, and defines dictionary advance values; §9.2.4 positions by widths. The font descriptor provides substitution information but does not specify an algorithm for substitute outline shaping. Condensing a chosen substitute to widths is ADR 0358 policy, not an explicit normative signature.
features.verdict: Direct outline-width/height expectations use deterministic Times-Roman and explicit 722 versus 361 em-width values, and the model-level witness checks width bounds against stated widths plus an independent /StemV check. These are more than assertion of the derived stretch value. However, the behavior of the scale itself remains the documented ADR 0358 choice because the clause binds widths/displacement, not exact substituted contours.
features.test_changes_since_prior: The new unreadable-program tests exercise marks/text but do not assert advance geometry. refused_font_metrics.rs replaced visible placement checks with direct metrics_only advance checks (800/1000 and default zero), while adding refusal/substitute wording assertions. Existing substituted_shapes and simple_font_widths tests provide geometric/consumer checks outside the new additions.
residuals: No current assigned test compares a malformed embedded-program fixture's rendered glyph origins and pixels against an exact-xref otherwise-identical font with the FontFile key removed.
The arbitrary stretch policy boundaries (median, scale floor, condense-only) are not normative obligations; retain as ratified ADR scope.

features.normative_effect: For converter output, preserve the selected fitting in the embedded CFF/OpenType program. PDF text positioning still uses dictionary advances; CFF charstrings also state widths, while OpenType hmtx carries advances. Exact CFF restatement strategy and rounding/refusal limits are implementation choices constrained by preservation requirements.
features.verdict: The writer has direct synthetic expected charstring bytes, width-preservation tests, and read-back over every glyph of shipped faces; it does not rely on a different renderer. Runtime substitute outline scaling is independently exercised by the deterministic simple-font outline extent test. The archive integration assertion is a selected representative integration, while library readback covers shipped face glyphs.
features.test_changes_since_prior: CFF Type 2 charstring scaling and OpenType wrapper fitting tests are new in this range, plus CFF restatement machinery; no tests here establish a PDF-standard-mandated substituted shape.
residuals: The proof criterion permits only missing zero-length horizontal lines; that is implementation proof policy and should stay separate from a claim that ISO prescribes contour-by-contour scaling.
No added independent PDF viewer rendering comparison is appropriate or used as normative evidence.

features.normative_effect: For Type 1 fonts using CFF tables, glyph descriptions are found using §9.6.5.2 name encoding, not the TrueType/cmap route. This is direct explicit processor routing language.
features.verdict: Direct public-PDF coverage exists and is strong: exact xref is asserted, embedded synthetic OpenType CFF uses a `post` v3 table without names and a conflicting Macintosh cmap, while PDF Differences request suffixed names; selected GIDs `[2, 1]` distinguish encoding-name→CFF-charset from cmap selection or suffix stripping. Bare Type1C control uses the same CFF bytes and reaches the same glyph IDs. The current code follows §9.9.1's explicit Type 1/CFF routing bullet. Test existed before this code comparison; no test edits in the changed range.
features.test_changes_since_prior: No changes to opentype_selection_audit.rs in 4015a9ae..b901326c; its current exact-xref assertions directly exercise this newly added branch and serve as a control.
